sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cathubodua is a Gaulish goddess. Her cult appears in the Haute-Savoie region of France. The tribal name Boduogenos carries her root. It means 'people of Bodua'. Writers tie Cathubodua to the war goddess Badb. Black-robed women copied the Badb in battle. These women acted as druids. They stood on the sidelines and screamed. The screams drove the warriors onward. People saw this at the ruin of the druidic college at Anglesey. Scholars debate whether the Badb began as a Celtic or pre-Celtic figure. Her bird form may come from a Neolithic goddess of the same shape.
